The man plunged the kitchen knife he was holding into my stomach.
(It hurts☆)
A burning pain shot through me.
Hot blood poured out, and I could tell I was hurtling straight toward certain death.{p}
rows.48:22c0:
I got sleepy, too.
I was only in junior high, after all.
By the time I rubbed my drowsy eyes and looked at the clock with my head all foggy, it was already past midnight.
That was way too late, any way you look at it.
I was just thinking, how could the parents put up with this, when he finally came out.{p}
rows.49:2cdc:
"I couldn't see their faces. Could you, Orihara?"
Hirooka asked anxiously.
She only shook her head quietly.
At that, he made his decision.
He would keep quiet.
"Let's keep this a secret between just the two of us. That way, they're sure to convince themselves they were mistaken about seeing us.
And then they won't have to suffer any misfortune, will they?"
By saying so, Hirooka convinced himself as well.
In fact, perhaps that really was the best thing.
Orihara, too, decided to go along with Hirooka.
And so the two of them came to share a secret.
Having a secret of your own, just between two people, is important, you know.
When a man and a woman share a secret, their relationship moves forward quickly.
Perhaps the legend of the cherry tree was born from that very idea in the first place.
And then they parted, promising that tomorrow night, without fail, they would confirm their love once more.{p}
